games.title: Dream Quest
games.note: Made alone by Peter Whalen, with famously rough art; he later joined Blizzard's Hearthstone team.

games.title: Dominion
games.dev: Donald X. Vaccarino / Rio Grande Games
games.note: The card game that started deck-building as a genre; it won the 2009 Spiel des Jahres.

games.title: Android: Netrunner
games.dev: Fantasy Flight Games (Richard Garfield and Lukas Litzsinger)
games.note: Fantasy Flight's revival of Richard Garfield's 1996 Netrunner, a hacker-versus-corporation card duel.

games.title: Magic: The Gathering
games.dev: Richard Garfield / Wizards of the Coast
games.note: Richard Garfield's 1993 game created the collectible card game.

games.title: Monster Train 2
games.note: Released in May 2025 under Big Fan Games, a Devolver Digital label.

games.title: Inscryption
games.note: Began as Sacrifices Must Be Made, Daniel Mullins's entry for the Ludum Dare 43 game jam in 2018.

games.title: Balatro
games.note: Started as an online version of the Cantonese card game Big Two; it sold over five million copies by January 2025.

games.title: Poker
games.note: The earliest specific account is English actor Joe Cowell's description of a 20-card game on a steamboat in 1829.

games.title: Luck Be a Landlord
games.note: A slot-machine deckbuilder about paying rising rent; Balatro's creator called it his largest inspiration. Early access began in 2021.

games.title: Peglin
games.note: Began at a 48-hour game jam themed Fall; early access ran from 2022 until the full release in 2024.

games.title: Dicey Dungeons
games.note: Irish designer Terry Cavanagh's dice-rolling roguelike, with music by Chipzel.

games.title: Vampire Survivors
games.note: Luca Galante started it in 2020 while unemployed; it won the BAFTA for Best Game in 2023.

games.title: Brotato
games.note: A solo game by Thomas Gervraud, named after the Rambo-style heroes of Broforce; early access began in 2022.

games.title: Halls of Torment
games.note: Its pitch: if Diablo was a three-course meal, Halls of Torment would be a candy bar.

games.title: Ball x Pit
games.note: Kenny Sun started it after playing the mobile game Punball in 2021; it passed a million copies in December 2025.

games.title: Marvel Snap
games.note: Second Dinner was founded by former Hearthstone developers, including Ben Brode and Hamilton Chu.

games.title: Blue Prince
games.note: Tonda Ros drew on Christopher Manson's puzzle book Maze, and later commissioned Manson to contribute art and a puzzle.

links.took: Building a deck during play by adding cards one at a time.
links.added: A single-player roguelike climb where the deck grows after every fight.

src.t: Wikipedia: Slay the Spire, citing Rock Paper Shotgun, 2018

links.extra: Casey Yano named Dominion, Ascension and the PC game Dream Quest as the core influences.

links.took: A solo roguelike deckbuilder: fight with cards, then add new ones as you descend.
links.added: A branching map, relics, enemies that show their next move, and polished art.

links.took: Card-game design sense from a game Anthony Giovannetti played a lot.
links.added: Single-player card battles against monsters instead of a human rival.

src.t: Wikipedia: Slay the Spire, citing Rock Paper Shotgun, 2018

links.extra: Giovannetti said he played a lot of Magic growing up and a lot of Netrunner.

links.took: The feel of playing cards that Giovannetti grew up with, captured digitally.
links.added: Automated rules and a single-player roguelike climb.

links.took: Richard Garfield, Magic's designer, who also created the original 1996 Netrunner.
links.added: An asymmetric hacker-versus-corporation duel, sold in fixed sets rather than random packs.

links.took: The fight-then-upgrade structure of an early roguelike deckbuilder.
links.added: Dice instead of cards, slotted into equipment to trigger effects.

links.took: Rogue popularized descending through random dungeons with permanent death.
links.added: Every fight is played with a deck of cards you build as you go.

links.took: Slay the Spire popularized the roguelike deckbuilder.
links.added: Defending a train's floors with units and spells, pairing two monster clans each run.

links.took: Multi-floor card battles and clan pairings.
links.added: A new campaign and clans, published by Devolver's Big Fan Games label.

links.took: Sacrificing creatures to pay for stronger ones.
links.added: A card game in a dark cabin against a captor, with escape-room puzzles.

src.t: Wikipedia: Inscryption, citing Daniel Mullins in Game Rant

links.took: Daniel Mullins's fourth-wall-breaking horror and secrets hidden beneath the game.
links.added: A card game at the center of the same meta-mystery style.

links.took: A branching map between card battles, like Slay the Spire's.
links.added: Sacrifice-based combat and a horror story outside the card table.

links.took: Four themed bosses, which Daniel Mullins likened to Pokémon gym leaders.
links.added: Each Scrybe rules a different style of card play.

links.took: A roguelike with no enemy, where you just chase a high score through combos.
links.added: Poker hands and jokers that bend the scoring rules.
links.extra: LocalThunk came across it through a Northernlion stream and watched videos of it rather than playing it.

links.took: Poker's hand rankings: pairs, straights, flushes and full houses.
links.added: Jokers that multiply scores, and escalating blinds you must beat to survive.

src.t: PC Gamer, I don't play poker at all, says solo developer

links.extra: LocalThunk based it on Big Two, a Cantonese card game built on poker hands, and says he doesn't play poker.

links.took: Only ideas for controller support; LocalThunk played it near the end of development.
links.added: Everything else: he avoided deckbuilders so he wouldn't borrow their ideas.

src.t: GamesRadar+, Balatro's creator had never played Slay the Spire, 2024

links.extra: Often assumed to be a source, but LocalThunk says he cut himself off from roguelikes while designing Balatro.

links.took: Always-active relics, which Dan DiIorio prefers over cards in a deck.
links.added: A slot machine you build symbol by symbol to pay rising rent.

src.t: Dan DiIorio, Questions and Danswers, TrampolineTales blog

links.took: Aiming a ball into a field of pegs and watching it bounce.
links.added: Each shot is an attack on monsters in a roguelike run.

src.t: Wikipedia: Peglin, citing Red Nexus Games in TouchArcade, 2023

links.took: A branching map, relics and upgrades over a run.
links.added: Orbs launched like pachinko balls instead of cards.

src.t: Wikipedia: Peglin, citing Red Nexus Games in TouchArcade, 2023

links.took: Its launch-and-watch style, which first inspired the jam game.
links.added: Pachinko pegs and a goblin hero fighting monsters.

src.t: Wikipedia: Peglin, citing Red Nexus Games in TouchArcade, 2023

links.took: Roguelike deckbuilder structure: fights, rewards and a growing set of tools.
links.added: A backpack grid where item placement decides how items work.

src.t: Wikipedia: Backpack Hero, citing Jasper Cole in Shacknews, 2022

links.took: Clear, puzzle-like turn-based combat.
links.added: Inventory management as the battle system.

src.t: Wikipedia: Backpack Hero, citing Jasper Cole in Shacknews, 2022

links.took: A grid inventory where items take up space.
links.added: Items that power each other depending on where they sit.

src.t: Wikipedia: Backpack Hero, citing Jasper Cole in Shacknews, 2022

links.took: A briefcase-style grid inventory, as Rock Paper Shotgun noted.
links.added: Inventory as the whole game, with items boosting their neighbors.

src.t: Wikipedia: Backpack Hero, citing Rock Paper Shotgun, 2023

links.took: A hero who attacks automatically while you only steer.
links.added: Gothic pixel art, weapon evolutions and enormous hordes, for a few dollars.

src.t: PC Gamer, Vampire Survivors creator didn't have a vision

links.extra: Luca Galante said his first prototype played exactly like Magic Survival, a 2019 mobile game.

links.took: Gothic monsters and vampire hunters, via a Castlevania-style asset pack.
links.added: Auto-attacking horde survival; Konami later licensed an official Castlevania expansion in 2024.
links.extra: Galante called the 2024 Ode to Castlevania expansion a full circle moment.

links.took: Rogue popularized runs that end in permanent death, with random upgrades along the way.
links.added: Thirty-minute survival runs where you only move and weapons fire on their own.

links.took: The auto-attacking, wave-survival formula Vampire Survivors popularized.
links.added: Short arena waves with a shop between them, and up to six weapons at once.

src.t: Gamesear, Brotato: a Vampire Survivors-inspired arena shooter

links.took: Its biggest influence: auto-attacking survival against hordes.
links.added: Action RPG character building and a 1990s isometric look.

src.t: Wikipedia: Halls of Torment, citing Chasing Carrots' interview with Pieuvre, 2024

links.took: A gothic, hellish isometric world and loot-driven progression.
links.added: Shrunk into short survivors-style runs: Diablo as a candy bar.

src.t: Wikipedia: Halls of Torment, citing creative director Paul Lawitzki, 2024

links.took: Deep action RPG systems, which the team set out to shrink into a pocket version.
links.added: Horde survival runs instead of a sprawling online world.

links.took: The look of old-school isometric RPGs, alongside Arcanum, Nox and Planescape: Torment.
links.added: Those visuals applied to a survivors-style horde game.

links.took: The Vampire Survivors structure, which Funday adopted as a well-tested base.
links.added: Deep Rock's dwarves, digging through rock, and extraction by drop pod.

src.t: GamesRadar+, Anders Leicht Rohde (Funday Games) in Edge

links.extra: Rohde said Ghost Ship's founders were keen Vampire Survivors players.

links.took: Bouncing balls into rows of targets, block-breaker style.
links.added: The targets are advancing monsters, and every ball is a weapon.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ball x Pit, citing Game Informer, 2025

links.took: Vampire Survivors popularized collecting gems to level up during a run.
links.added: Brick-breaker aiming, plus a village you build between runs.

links.took: Breakout popularized the paddle, the ball and the wall of bricks.
links.added: Power-ups falling from bricks, enemies, and many designed levels.

links.took: Former Hearthstone developers, including Ben Brode, who founded Second Dinner.
links.added: Three-minute matches over three locations, and a snap to double the stakes.

links.took: Ideas from its quick mobile matches, part of the designers' grocery-cart mix.
links.added: Superhero cards and turns played simultaneously.

src.t: Wikipedia: Marvel Snap, citing the GDC talk Designing Marvel Snap, 2023

links.extra: The designers also drew on Backgammon's doubling cube and Paul Peterson's card game Smash Up.

links.took: Magic popularized collectible card battles with mana, creatures and spells.
links.added: A free digital card game with automated rules and random effects.

links.took: Playing it pushed Tonda Ros to try his own puzzle ideas in Unity.
links.added: A manor drafted room by room, rebuilt every day.

links.took: Exploring a house for its story, which also spurred Ros to start building.
links.added: A mansion that changes daily and a mystery spread across its rooms.

links.took: Drafting: choosing one option from a small, random selection.
links.added: Drafting rooms instead of cards to shape the house.

src.t: Wikipedia: Blue Prince, citing The New York Times and GameReactor

links.took: Clues scattered in distant places, without needing all of them to progress.
links.added: A manor that resets every day.

links.took: Rogue popularized layouts randomized anew on each run.
links.added: Each day the manor resets and you draft its rooms again.
